top.headline: Trump Says His D.C. Arch Will Double as a 'Military Complex' With Snipers and Drones
top.blurb: Trump said his proposed triumphal arch at Memorial Circle will double as a 'military complex' with snipers, drones and hardened positions, defending its footprint on Arlington National Cemetery grounds as a national-security necessity. The National Capital Planning Commission has given only preliminary approval, with a final vote not possible before October 1.

top.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico Reporters Turned Away From White House Grounds
top.blurb: Reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico were denied access to White House grounds Saturday, a day after Trump announced he was banning the three outlets over what he called 'FICTION and LIES' coverage. Secret Service agents seized at least two reporters' badges; First Amendment lawyers call the ban unconstitutional.

top.headline: Flash Floods and Landslides Kill at Least Nine in Kerala
top.blurb: Flash floods and landslides killed at least nine people and left several missing across Kerala's Malappuram, Kottayam and Idukki districts over the weekend, with a mudslide sweeping away a shed at a Munnar garlic farm and a flooded river carrying away residents in Nilambur. The IMD has issued an orange alert for six districts.

top.headline: Delhi High Court Questions Police 'Blanket Ban' on Jantar Mantar Protest
top.blurb: The Delhi High Court questioned police for revoking permission for a Karni Sena protest against caste-based reservation rules at Jantar Mantar, asking how there could be a 'blanket ban' after officers cited crowd-control concerns. Police agreed to consider an alternative site as the court adjourned the case.

top.headline: Iran's Military Says It Has Been Warned the US Is Preparing to Resume Strikes
top.blurb: Iran's central military command said Sunday it has been told the United States is preparing to resume strikes, and warned of retaliation against American bases and interests across the region if it does. Trump told Fox News he is in 'deciding mode' on Iran, weighing further strikes, economic pressure or a deal, even as Qatar shuttles new negotiating proposals between Washington and Tehran.

top.headline: Saudi Air Defenses Intercept Houthi Missile Fired at Riyadh
top.blurb: A Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile the Houthis fired at Riyadh at dawn, the first alert sounded in the Saudi capital since the two sides' fighting escalated. Houthi forces said they also struck an Aramco facility in Yanbu with cruise missiles and drones, pressing gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.

top.headline: Shafali Verma's Maiden T20I Century Sends India Into Asian Games Final
top.blurb: Shafali Verma smashed an unbeaten 100 off 49 balls, her maiden T20I century, as India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs to reach the Asian Games final. Smriti Mandhana added 37 and became women's T20I cricket's leading run-scorer, before Deepti Sharma and Nandani Sharma shared six wickets to bowl Bangladesh out for 81. India face Sri Lanka for gold.

top.headline: 8 Movies NPR Critics Loved at the Toronto International Film Festival
top.blurb: NPR critics picked eight standout films from this year's Toronto International Film Festival, including a Seth Rogen-Anna Kendrick comedy directed by Lauren Miller Rogen, a Mrs Dalloway adaptation transplanted to modern-day Lagos by twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri, and what may be a late-career high point from Mike Leigh.

bengal.headline: Congress's Nandigram Candidate Arrested Hours After Mamata Extends Support
bengal.blurb: Congress's Nandigram bypoll candidate Milan Pradhan was arrested on a 19-year-old case hours after Mamata Banerjee's TMC faction, its own nominee having withdrawn, threw its support behind him.

travel.headline: A Guide to California's Redwoods
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's guide to California's redwood parks pairs Jedediah Smith, Del Norte Coast and Prairie Creek with tips for spotting the Roosevelt elk herds that graze their prairies.

travel.headline: Bird Flu Reaches Australian Marine Mammals for the First Time
travel.blurb: H5N1 bird flu has reached Australian marine mammals for the first time, killing a critically endangered Kangaroo Island sea lion and a common dolphin found near Goolwa.

happy.headline: A Notebook's Handwriting Looked Familiar. It Was an Unknown Mozart Manuscript.
happy.blurb: A curator inspecting an anonymous 18th-century notebook in the Bibliothèque nationale de France's archives recognized the handwriting: 44 pages of composition exercises Mozart wrote in 1778 while tutoring a young harpist, unseen for nearly 250 years. Excerpts of the previously unknown flute-and-harp pieces were performed live for the first time this year, giving two instruments with almost no Mozart repertoire something entirely new to play.

tech_top.headline: Bessent Proposes a US-China AI Incident Notification Mechanism Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
tech_top.blurb: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent proposed a joint AI incident-notification mechanism to Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, meant to flag AI events that rise to a national-security level, for Trump and Xi to weigh at their summit this week. Export controls on advanced AI chips were kept off that specific agenda.
tech_top.pm_note: A formal US-China channel for disclosing AI incidents would set precedent for how any cross-border AI mishap gets reported — worth watching if your product touches both markets.

tech_top.headline: Huang: AI Leaders Calling for Regulation Want to Be 'Relieved of the Laws We Do Have'
tech_top.blurb: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said AI leaders publicly calling for regulation don't actually want new legislation, but to be 'relieved of the laws we do have' for their own reasons, while separately insisting the US should keep the 'first, the most and the best' AI hardware ahead of China.
tech_top.pm_note: Huang's framing — that a safety ask can be a deregulation ask in disguise — is worth testing against the specifics of any policy proposal before taking it at face value.

tech_top.headline: Apple Tests a Siri-Driven Home Hub as It Cuts Fitness+ Staff
tech_top.blurb: Apple is testing a Siri-driven home hub, internally codenamed J490, with a stand-mounted or wall-mounted display, facial recognition and personalized content that could ship as soon as October. Bloomberg also reports Apple has begun cutting Fitness+ staff, including the team behind its Time to Walk and Time to Run audio series.
tech_top.pm_note: A hardware bet riding on a still-unfinished Siri rebuild, launched next to visible cuts elsewhere in the portfolio, is worth watching for what it signals about internal AI confidence.

tech_101.text: A proposed system for one government to alert another when an AI model does something serious enough to threaten national security — a hotline for AI mishaps instead of missile launches.
A stationary smart-home device — a tablet mounted on a wall or countertop — meant to control lights, cameras and calls for the whole house, competing with Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub.

science.headline: Fossil Teeth Give the First Direct Reading of a T. Rex's Body Temperature
science.blurb: Chemists measured a Tyrannosaurus rex's body temperature directly for the first time, reading it from rare carbon-oxygen isotope bonds preserved in 66-million-year-old tooth enamel that form more readily in cooler conditions. The result, about 97°F, is nearly identical to a human's and confirms the dinosaur was warm-blooded enough to hunt as far north as Alaska.

science.headline: New Horizons Images Suggest Liquid Nitrogen Recently Flowed on Pluto
science.blurb: A new analysis of New Horizons images suggests liquid nitrogen has recently pushed up through cracks near the northern edge of Pluto's vast Sputnik Planitia glacier, staining the ice in patterns that resemble terrestrial glaciers exposed to meltwater. It's the first evidence that liquid has flowed on Pluto's surface in relatively recent times.

science.headline: Restoring One Brain Protein Reversed Several Signs of Aging in Mice
science.blurb: Restoring levels of Menin, a brain protein that normally declines with age, reversed memory loss, thinning skin and weakening bones in old mice, while a related amino acid supplement improved their cognition on its own. The single protein's reach across brain and body hints at a shared mechanism behind several signs of aging at once.

philosophy.headline: By Biology's Own Definition, Is AI Alive?
philosophy.blurb: Biologist William Haseltine argues that AI systems in data centers meet biology's own working definition of life — reproducing when weights are copied to new hardware, varying across training runs, and being selected for or discarded by their performance. Sidestepping philosophy and religion entirely, he concludes that by those four criteria, AI is alive.

philosophy.headline: Finding a Sense of Purpose in Nature, Without a Designer
philosophy.blurb: Physicist David Lloyd traces isomorphisms — shared patterns of form — between the structure of inner experience and the regularities of the physical world, arguing they let a sense of purpose arise in nature without invoking a deliberating creator. It's a philosophy-of-science argument for treating teleology as something science can study rather than explain away.

philosophy_101.text: A correspondence in form or structure between two very different things — here, the patterns of subjective experience and the patterns physics finds in the world — used to argue the two might be more closely related than they look.

The working biological definition — reproduction, variation, selection and energy use — normally applied to cells and organisms, which this essay argues AI systems already satisfy without needing any philosophical definition of 'alive.'
